note: CANVAS-10: one autosave. It names the fields it touches and the WRITE REVISION it was based on; the server compares that with each touched field's last change (CANVAS-19), so a stale patch that touches untouched fields is rebased, not refused. It carries the type and the type version it was built against so that both sides can check every value before anything is written. The answer is the whole Document. A repeat of a patch that has already landed is a no-op, not a conflict (1kg.5.2).

valid.name: several fields flushed together before an AI edit starts (CANVAS-24)
renaming is an ordinary field write (LIB-15)
an integral number is an integer however it is spelled: JavaScript cannot tell 14.0 from 14
session notes, every field of the type in one autosave

fields.recap: They found the ledger, and then the tide found them.

valid.name: a quest log thread moved to resolved
a stat block's speed alone: a patch need not mention a required field
a stat block's armour class, set to a new number

invalid.name: a patch that touches nothing
invalid.why: a no-op is decided by the server comparing values, not sent as an empty patch

invalid.name: clearing a stat block's armour class
invalid.why: LIB-12: ac is required on a stat block, so an autosave of an emptied AC cell is refused rather than storing a document the record calls invalid

invalid.name: clearing a stat block's hit points
invalid.why: LIB-12 names all three, and the stat_block_card renderer is handed hp as a required integer

invalid.name: a negative armour class in an autosave
invalid.why: 1kg.5.7, F-10: statblock.ac is floored at 0 by its own per-field bounds, inside the integer kind's own range

invalid.name: a party level of zero
invalid.why: 1kg.5.7, F-10: there is no level 0, so encounter.party_level starts at 1

invalid.name: no base revision
invalid.why: CANVAS-34: without a base the server cannot tell a stale write from a fresh one, and a stale write must never overwrite newer work

invalid.name: the handoff's version id as the base
invalid.why: CANVAS-34: a history version is never a concurrency token

invalid.name: a field the type does not declare
invalid.why: 1kg.5.2: invalid-field cases fail before writes. A request is strict on both sides, because the client built it

invalid.name: the handoff's camelCase key
invalid.why: snake_case on the wire: if_attacked

invalid.name: a key named __proto__ among the fields
invalid.why: not declared, like any stray key. JSON.parse makes it an ordinary own key, which a record parser then drops silently; the client must refuse it where the server would, not lose it on the way

invalid.name: a key named __proto__ beside the fields
invalid.why: a request is strict; a key JavaScript treats specially is still a stray key

invalid.name: a base revision that is not an integer
invalid.why: 14.5 is not a count of writes; only an integral number is an integer

invalid.name: clearing the name
invalid.why: the one field that cannot be empty

invalid.name: a prose field of 20,001 characters
invalid.why: RAIL-6: caps are checked before any write or provider work

invalid.name: a portrait by URL
invalid.why: X-10: assets are named by id

invalid.name: an author claimed by the client
invalid.why: CANVAS-10: a direct patch is recorded as author gm by the server; authorship is never the client's to state

invalid.name: a reveal mask smuggled into a save
invalid.why: X-2: nothing reaches a player except through the reveal mutation; an autosave can never widen what the table sees

invalid.name: no type
invalid.why: values are checked against the type's field kinds on both sides, before the write

invalid.name: an armour class written as text
invalid.why: 1kg.5.3: an integer field takes a JSON integer. "12" is not one, and neither is true — Pydantic would otherwise read true as 1

invalid.name: an ability the rules do not have
invalid.why: 1kg.5.3: the ability block has a closed key set (str, dex, con, int, wis, cha). In a request the client builds, a stray key is a bug on both sides

invalid.name: a prototype key smuggled into an ability block
invalid.why: The known pitfall: JSON allows an own __proto__ key and a plain-object lookup would find a function. refusingProtoKeys recurses so a nested one is refused before any field schema sees it

invalid.name: a trait with no name
invalid.why: 1kg.5.3: an entry_list entry is {name, text}, and the name is what a renderer shows as its heading, so it cannot be blank

invalid.name: a trait carrying a key the entry does not declare
invalid.why: 1kg.5.3, ED-2: an entry_list is ONE field and nothing addresses inside it, so its entries are closed too. In a request both sides refuse the key

invalid.name: a session number that is text
invalid.why: 1kg.5.3: session is an integer field

invalid.name: a character sheet's speed as a number
invalid.why: speed is text because it reads '30 ft.', and a text field never takes a number on either side
